name: CTI Enrichment - Wazuh + AbuseIPDB + Cloud + Slack

nodes.name: 01 - Webhook (Wazuh Ingestion)
nodes.notes:
STEP 1 - INGESTION
Receive raw alert payload from Wazuh.
Expected fields: rule.id, data.srcip, agent.name, rule.description, timestamp

nodes.name: 02 - Parse & Extract IP
nodes.notes:
STEP 2A - PARSE
Validates and normalizes the IP from the raw Wazuh payload.
Throws error if IP is malformed.

nodes.name: 03 - AbuseIPDB CTI Query
nodes.notes:
STEP 2B - CTI ENRICHMENT
Queries AbuseIPDB for threat intel on the IP.
Returns: abuseConfidenceScore, totalReports, countryCode, usageType, isp, domain

⚠️ CREDENTIAL REQUIRED: AbuseIPDB API Key
Get your free key at: https://www.abuseipdb.com/account/api

nodes.name: 04 - Merge CTI + Alert Data
nodes.notes:
STEP 2C - MERGE
Combines the AbuseIPDB CTI data with the original Wazuh alert.
Calculates risk classification: CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW

nodes.name: 05 - Score >= 80? (Risk Gate)
nodes.notes:
STEP 3 - RISK GATE
Routes flow based on abuseConfidenceScore:
• TRUE (>=80): HIGH RISK path → Cloud verification + urgent alert
• FALSE (<80): LOW RISK path → Informational log only

Threshold 80 chosen based on AbuseIPDB documentation:
scores above 80 indicate consistent malicious reporting history.

nodes.name: 06 - AWS: Check EC2/VPC Interaction
nodes.notes:
STEP 3A - CLOUD CONTEXT (HIGH RISK PATH)
Queries AWS EC2 API to check if the malicious IP
has interacted with any VPC Network Interfaces.

⚠️ CREDENTIAL REQUIRED: AWS Access Key + Secret
Needed permissions: ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces

💡 ALTERNATIVE: Replace with GCP API or Azure equivalent.
This node is interchangeable based on your cloud provider.

nodes.name: 07 - Parse Cloud Context
nodes.notes:
STEP 3B - NORMALIZE CLOUD RESPONSE
Parses the AWS API response and identifies
which EC2/VPC assets the malicious IP interacted with.

Outputs:
• cloudTouched: boolean
• affectedAssets: list of EC2 instances/interfaces
• escalationNeeded: true if cloud assets were touched

nodes.name: 08 - Build Slack Alert (HIGH RISK)
nodes.notes:
STEP 4A - FORMAT ALERT (HIGH RISK)
Builds a rich Slack Block Kit message with:
• Full CTI data from AbuseIPDB
• Affected cloud assets list
• One-click action buttons:
  - Block IP on Firewall
  - View on AbuseIPDB
  - Open JIRA ticket

⚠️ CUSTOMIZE: Replace firewall URL and JIRA URL.

nodes.name: 09 - Send Slack Alert (HIGH RISK)
nodes.notes:
STEP 4B - SEND ALERT (HIGH RISK)
Posts the formatted Block Kit message to Slack.

⚠️ CREDENTIAL REQUIRED: Slack Incoming Webhook URL
Create at: https://api.slack.com/apps → Incoming Webhooks

💡 ALTERNATIVE: Replace with Microsoft Teams webhook
using the 'Microsoft Teams' n8n node.

parameters.responseBody: ={"status": "processed", "riskLevel": "{{ $('04 - Merge CTI + Alert Data').first().json.riskLevel }}", "ip": "{{ $('04 - Merge CTI + Alert Data').first().json.suspiciousIP }}", "action": "alert_sent_to_slack"}

nodes.name: 10 - Respond to Wazuh (HIGH RISK)
nodes.notes:
STEP 5A - WEBHOOK RESPONSE (HIGH RISK)
Returns HTTP 200 to Wazuh confirming the alert was processed.
Payload includes risk level and action taken.

nodes.name: 11 - Log Low Risk Alert
nodes.notes:
STEP 4C - LOW RISK PATH
For IPs with score < 80, sends a lightweight
informational log to a secondary Slack channel (#soc-logs).

No action buttons — purely for audit trail.

nodes.name: 12 - Send Log to #soc-logs
nodes.notes:
STEP 4D - SEND LOG (LOW RISK PATH)
Posts informational message to #soc-logs channel.
Same webhook as the main alert, different channel.

parameters.responseBody: ={"status": "processed", "riskLevel": "{{ $('04 - Merge CTI + Alert Data').first().json.riskLevel }}", "ip": "{{ $('04 - Merge CTI + Alert Data').first().json.suspiciousIP }}", "action": "logged_only"}

nodes.name: 13 - Respond to Wazuh (LOW RISK)
nodes.notes:
STEP 5B - WEBHOOK RESPONSE (LOW RISK)
Returns HTTP 200 to Wazuh confirming the alert
was received and logged. No escalation triggered.
